mcp.name: MCP
mcp.description: Lets AI assistants such as Claude Desktop and Claude Code work with your collection, and connects external MCP servers.

allow_writes.label: Let MCP clients make changes
allow_writes.description: Off: assistants can only read (list decks, search, read notes).

mcp.heading: Assistants (MCP)
mcp.subtitle: Connect an AI assistant such as Claude so it can read your decks and add cards for you. Set it up once; most people only need the first tab.

connect.intro: The assistant opens this profile's collection through a small command-line program called fc. Pick your assistant, paste the setting below into it, and you're done.
connect.client_hint: The setting differs a little for each one. "Other" covers any app that supports MCP (Cursor, VS Code, …).

fc_missing.label: The fc program was not found
fc_missing.description: The assistant needs the command-line tool fc. The installed app ships it next to itself; here it is neither next to this app nor on your PATH (running a development build? Build it first with `cargo build -p fc-cli`). Type its full path here and the setting below updates itself. Without it the setting just says "fc", which only works once fc is on your PATH.

connect.db_unknown: This app was not started as the desktop app, so the collection file's location is unknown: replace the path in the setting with your collection.db.

claude_desktop.open: In Claude Desktop, open Settings → Developer → Edit Config.
claude_desktop.paste: Copy the text below and paste it into that file. If the file already has "mcpServers", add only the "flashcard" part inside it.
claude_desktop.restart: Save the file, quit Claude Desktop completely (also from the system tray) and open it again.

claude_code.open: Open a terminal (PowerShell on Windows, Terminal on macOS).
claude_code.paste: Copy the command below, paste it into the terminal and press Enter. Once is enough.
claude_code.restart: Start Claude Code again. Typing /mcp in it should show flashcard as connected.

other.open: In your client's settings, add a new MCP server of type "stdio" (a command it starts).
other.paste: Put the program into the "command" field and the rest into "arguments", one per line. If it wants JSON, use the Claude Desktop text instead.

connect.copied: Copied. Now paste it into your assistant.
connect.copy_failed: Could not copy: select the text and copy it yourself.
connect.test_hint: Ask your assistant: "List my decks." If it names your decks, the connection works. If it doesn't, check the paths in the setting and restart the assistant.

server.heading: What the assistant can do
server.intro: Only the jobs listed here. It can never delete anything, and every change it makes is an ordinary step you can undo in the app.
server.read_only_on: The assistant can see your decks and cards but cannot change anything: the tools that change things are not even offered to it.
server.read_only_off: The assistant can also add decks and cards and edit notes. It still cannot delete, and you can undo each change.
server.read_only_example: On: if you say "add these words to my deck", the assistant replies that it may only read.

client.heading: External MCP servers
client.intro: On the first tab an assistant uses this app; here it is the other way round: the app uses other programs. The app's AI features (for example when they write cards for you) may call the tools of the servers you add here, such as reading files on your computer or fetching text from a notes app.
client.name: Name
client.confirm_add: This app will start the following program whenever its AI features use this server: {command}. Only continue if you trust it.
client.confirm_approve: This server came from outside (a restored backup, for example) and has never been approved. Approving lets the app start: {command}. Only continue if you trust it.
client.when: You only need this if you want the AI features to reach such sources. If not, leave it empty: nothing else depends on it.
client.safety: A server is a program that runs on your computer with your permissions. The app starts it only after you approve its exact command, and tools that change things ask first. Add only servers you installed yourself and trust.
client.add_hint: The server's own instructions tell you the command and its arguments (e.g. npx and -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem).

validation.mcp_server: Check the server: it needs a name, and a command (or an http(s) URL).

not_found.mcp_server: That MCP server no longer exists.

conflict.mcp_server_name: Another MCP server already has this name.

permission.mcp_read_only: MCP clients may only read: changes are turned off.
